Highly recommended...with some reservations. Surprisingly deep storyline for a casually simple "hacking game". Still hellalot buggy though so expect to restart at least a few times.

THE GOOD
I came into this game fresh - I knew it was a "hacking game" and that's pretty much it. 

The main storyline is surprisingly deep for something that I thought was a simple hacking game. There's a bit of a mystery over what happened to Bit and it's actually a bit of a heartwrencher at the end even though (minor spoilers) [spoiler] you know that Bit is already dead at the start of the game [/spoiler].

The game starts you off with easy, low-risk missions just to ease you into it. Once you get further along, it gets more interesting because there's a time crunch to do what you need to do before someone tracks you and your computer shuts down.

Just like real life, the game allows for multiple ways for you to do something. For example, instead of hacking into XXX's PC to get something, you can also get it by doing other things, or by hacking into another person's PC. It keeps it surprisingly fresh through multiple playthroughs. And you get to satisfy voyeuristic tendencies by snooping through people's  private files while you're in the system...or just delete everything and imagine the crash and burn.


NEUTRAL
Also like real life, if you accidentally delete everything from your (fake) computer, the (fake) system crashes and you might have to restart your whole game. Or if you accidentally deleted that super important file that has the info that your client wanted...yep, it's gone now. You gonna have to abort your contract. If it's from the main story line, there's no way that I found that will trigger the next sequence.  I hope you saved before doing that...or you gotta have to Google it.

And there's other pretty great stuff too...I'll let you explore those.

The game doesn't offer much of a challenge. Yes, there's that time crunch factor for the harder missions but there are certain features in the game that makes it surprisingly easy. Not sure whether it's a bug or not but (minor spoilers) [spoiler] if you are hacking into some terminals and you disconnect halfway, some of the ports you've hacked into previously will remain open. This also happens if your computer crashed because time ran out. [/spoiler].


THE BAD
It's still pretty buggy. In some cases, unless you follow the instructions exactly, it might not trigger the next sequence of the game (e.g. if you skipped ahead and hacked some terminals before you're supposed to or if you've deleted some crucial files that you weren't supposed to delete). It doesn't always happen so it's a bit of a hit and miss. So expect at least a few restarts (I had to do it twice).

years past, and i am now a computer security architect which is why this game premise caught my eye. having to spend hours on Linux consoles most of my days i went in without any expectation for the game to really teach nothing about this but just as a fun time.

From the first moment, i was hooked. the simple game mechanism with the complying story and the fact that you really need to think your way through the later stage of the games made this game a treat.

I think this game is a great education for young people who usually don't have exposure to Linux/UNIX based computers which still use old style typing etc. and to basic computer networking concepts. 

The game will take you through the paces of learning what to do but will leave you to figure out what you need to do and that is a great change from modern games which focus more on graphics and hand-eye coordination and less about thinking. 

I recommend this game for those of you who want to have a glimpse on the world of network security

Okay, I've only played it for 9 hours, but by the time/cost calculation, it more than paid for itself. In fact, on full price it's really not bad (I got it in the sale for £3.49, half price).

Basically, this is a proper hacking sim, sort of. I mean, it's obviously not a full scale realistic version of hacking because it has stuff like a GUI and a magic password cracker, but these do get explained in the narrative. That aside, the commands you enter are real commands. And they have a real impact...
There's one particular mission, later on in the game, and it involves a very tough decision,[spoiler]you have to perform an assisted suicide for someone in a coma by breaking their pacemaker[/spoiler], I think I left the game running for a while so I could go and contemplate what to do over a green tea, but in the end I did what was asked of me, it still didn't feel good. I've rarely had that feeling in a game before. We [spoiler]kill[/spoiler] so often in games, but the immersiveness of this game made me feel so different. Damn...

It also has plenty of secrets and easter eggs, in fact, I know for a fact I haven't got all of them. The story path is probably about 10 hours, but like most puzzle games, that's longer or shorter depending on how good you are.

All in all, a highly reccomended purchase, especially with multiplayer possibly on the cards. When multiplayer comes out, remember 'openCDTray'.

Frankly, I usually don't write reviews. I don't find anything exceptional about most games to share my opinion. This one was different. Right off the bat, I was hooked. I went in expecting fast paced, Uplink style hacking. I was most definately not disappointed, but as soon as [spoiler]my screen BSODed from another hacker[/spoiler], I knew this game was diffferent. The intro was odd, but I rolled with it. I found the different challenges so varied, and interested in each one. It was not until later in the game, where the game started to test my morals and question the ethics of the hacking and technology industry in general where I got really hooked. I also find it very wonderful that they have other things to go back in and do again for another play through. Through my first five hours, I completed the game, and look forward to going back through and finishing the extras, including el's challenges.

One complaint, though. The "RAM" system for managing systems is hard to come to terms with. You will be frustrated as you can't seem to have quite enough RAM for that one other port hacking application. I ended up, by the end of the game, writing things down on a notepad next to me rather than using the built in note feature. Only ~750 MB of free RAM? You've got to be kidding me. I have over 16 GB free right now. Also, why do notes take up RAM? I understand why this is there, but it seems to be not quite as well thought out as well as it should have been.

All in all, it is well worth the five dollars I spent for it. I enjoyed it, and plan on enjoying it for much longer.

This is more of a simulation than a game that's actually fun to play. I much preferred Uplink.

The premise, that you play an elite hacker that depends entirely on donated scripts, is somewhat silly.

The graphics are non-existent, since the entire game is a slick imitation of a bash prompt.

The gameplay is incredibly easy.  Nearly every challenge involves typing a few commands and then quickly rummaging around file structures looking for clues.

The story is barely there, since it's built out of a string of terse e-mails.

Yet somehow this game is one of the few that pulls real emotions out of me.  Character death feels real because it's a plot point and not a gory spectacle.  Getting hacked feels shocking because the rest of the game is so hypnotic.  The story is interesting precisely because so many details are left to the imaginiation, but not to the point where there are huge holes in the plot.

It can be beaten in a few hours, but it's well worth several playthroughs.

Pretty sure this is the first review I've ever done. I'm going to avoid spoilers and keep it simple. 

Story 8/10
I found the story very intriguing and it grabbed me right away, I almost finished the game in one sessions because I was that engrossed with how it was turning out. I really do wish this game was more fleshed out in the way that you could go either white hat, gray hat, or black hat. Different routes would be absolutely AMAZING, but it doesn't take away from the game at all and it's 100% worth the price. Would love to enjoy more content from the creators.

Interface 7/10
The interface was simple yet during the more hectic missions it's complex enough that multitasking demanded my full attention in order to keep up. The nodes that you unlock can be a bit clustered at times, especially during the later stages of the game, would have liked to be able to map and place nodes in a way that I could organize it for ease of use.

Gameplay 9/10
Again, I had a metric shit ton of fun with this game. I would recommend that if you get stuck to think things through without gunning for a guide on the internet. I also would have loved to have been able to upgrade my hardware and software, but for a short game it's not needed at all (I think I finished the game in approx. 7 hours or so, I felt like I was really going through it kinda fast, but then again I do have knowledge in this field and I don't recall getting stuck for any long period of time.) I can't stress enough how much fun I had, I started this game around midnight and didn't even realize just how engrossed I was until I looked outside to see the sun had already risen.

TLDR
If you're in any way interested in the security field, I HIGHLY recommend picking this up. It was a blast to play and the price can't be beat. 5/7 would accidentally delete everyone's degrees again (OOPS :P)

I've been playing the Hacker Evolution games and was waiting for another similar game without the flaws. Hacknet is this game. It's a great combination of both fun and simulation. It FEELS like hacking, and the ambiance work is great.

-If you dislike typing commands, this isn't your game.

-If you're afraid of typing commands, this could interest you, as it's just a game and will have no real consequences, but is simulation enough for you to learn some things.

-If you like typing commands but don't do it often, and/or have just a tiny experience in hacking (like me), you'd love this game and will probably get some of the nods to real hacking events (the eOS logins, for instance)

-If you type commands everyday and program your own shell scripts, I'm not sure the game will be complex enough, as it's making great efforts to stay comprehensible for the average person. What I mean is, you won't program your own automated hacking software. You'll just download it from someone else's computer.

Looking back at it, it's a better game than I originally thought. The Junebug mission especially, without spoiling anything, is really intense and can even get a little thought provoking.
